topics.topic: (a) Computational design quality / aesthetic preference evaluation

sources.title: Calista: A deep learning-based system for understanding and evaluating website aesthetics
sources.key_idea: Proposes an automatic website-aesthetics evaluator built on deep-learning models that achieve high correlation with human perception, trained on two datasets (one with crowdsourced aesthetic ratings).
sources.takeaway: Automated scoring of website aesthetics that tracks human judgment is already SOTA-feasible (2023) and can serve directly as a quality gate in a generator pipeline.

sources.title: Predicting Visual Aesthetics Distributions of Mobile GUIs Using Deep Learning: The Appsthetics Histogram
sources.key_idea: Represents GUI visual aesthetics not as one score but as a distribution of individual raters; the median encodes degree of aesthetics, the average encodes consensus. A deep model predicts this distribution.
sources.takeaway: Aesthetic quality is user-dependent and multi-modal; anti-template gates should reason over rating distributions (dispersion = disagreement/diversity), not a single threshold.

sources.title: AesthetiQ: Enhancing Graphic Layout Design via Aesthetic-Aware Preference Alignment (AAPA)
sources.key_idea: Prior layout generators ignore the final rendered aesthetic; AAPA trains an MLLM for layout prediction using the MLLM's own aesthetic preferences via Direct Preference Optimization.
sources.takeaway: Aesthetic preference can be aligned into generation (not just measured post-hoc) via DPO; a generator can be steered toward human-like aesthetics while keeping outputs distinct.

sources.title: Unveiling the factors of aesthetic preferences with explainable AI
sources.key_idea: Uses multiple ML models on interpretable aesthetic attributes (color harmony, balance, etc.) to predict aesthetic scores, then SHAP to explain which attributes drive preference.
sources.takeaway: Aesthetic preference is decomposable into measurable attributes; these become the monitorable feature dimensions for an anti-template / quality gate.

sources.title: A computational framework for aesthetic preferences in architecture using computer vision and ANNs
sources.key_idea: Builds a computational-aesthetics framework (CV + artificial neural networks) to predict group aesthetic preference, grounded in part-to-whole theories from aesthetics and cognitive psychology.
sources.takeaway: Aesthetic prediction generalizes across design domains via part-to-whole composition modeling - the same CV/ANN approach transfers to web layout, typography and composition scoring.

topics.topic: (b) What distinguishes Awwwards / award-winning web design

sources.title: Award-Winning Web Design: Judging Criteria Decoded
sources.key_idea: Fewer than 365 of >15,000 yearly Awwwards submissions earn Site of the Day; criteria are published and scored across design, usability, creativity and content, and winning sites also outperform on engagement/conversion.
sources.takeaway: Awards are rubric-driven (design/usability/creativity/content + execution); a template cannot score on 'creativity/novelty' - the gate must measure originality explicitly.

sources.title: Award-winning website examples (what judges look for)
sources.key_idea: Breaks down actual Awwwards/Webby/CSS-Design-Awards winners, showing the design patterns and execution craft that separate memorable sites from forgettable ones.
sources.takeaway: Distinctiveness, narrative, bespoke interaction and execution quality are the differentiators; generic templates fail the 'memorable' bar on all of them.

sources.title: Best Of Design Awards 2025: Key Findings (DesignRush)
sources.key_idea: 2025 award winners favored clarity and restraint, with strong ideas outperforming decorative complexity; 'functional storytelling' and emotional intelligence defined the year more than novelty for its own sake.
sources.takeaway: Winning = clear narrative + emotional intelligence + restraint, not ornamentation; the anti-template system should reward coherent concept and storytelling, not merely 'busy' novelty.

sources.title: A Guide on Building Awwwards Worthy Websites
sources.key_idea: A practitioner account of the animation, interaction and cross-disciplinary (design + engineering + creative direction) craft behind an Awwwards-published portfolio.
sources.takeaway: Awwwards-level work fuses motion, interaction and technical craft - the structural opposite of static, Word-document-like templated layouts.

sources.title: How to Win an Awwward - lessons from a decade on Awwwards
sources.key_idea: Argues the winning combination is visual creativity plus technical craft, and that originality of concept, motion design and bespoke interaction are what set featured work apart.
sources.takeaway: Consistent differentiators are originality of concept, motion and bespoke interaction - the explicit anti-thesis of template/Word-document output.

topics.topic: (c) Novelty / diversity / distinctness metrics usable as automated gates

sources.title: DeCoDe Lab (MIT) - Design Diversity & Novelty Metrics
sources.key_idea: Consolidates metrics from design-methodology research for calculating diversity and novelty of designs, used when working with deep generative models that should produce diverse, novel designs.
sources.takeaway: An established metric toolkit exists (novelty = distance to nearest reference design; diversity = set-level dispersion) that maps directly onto anti-template gates.

sources.title: Beyond Statistical Similarity: Rethinking Metrics for Deep Generative Models in Engineering Design
sources.key_idea: Formalizes novelty as a point metric (dissimilarity of a sample from a reference/training set, e.g. nearest-neighbor distance) and diversity as a set metric (aggregate pairwise/coverage/entropy dispersion).
sources.takeaway: Define the anti-template gate as: novelty = min distance of a candidate to a corpus of prior/reference designs (must exceed threshold); diversity = dispersion/entropy across a batch.

sources.title: NoveltyBench: Evaluating Language Models for Humanlike Diversity
sources.key_idea: Shows SOTA models generate far less diversity than humans (fewer than ~4 distinct responses in 10 samples) using the distinct-k metric; novelty scales inversely with model size.
sources.takeaway: Off-the-shelf generators are biased toward low-diversity outputs - an explicit diversity gate (distinct-k / entropy) is necessary to avoid repetition across artifacts.

sources.title: DivGenBench: Measuring Generative Diversity (Preference Mode Collapse)
sources.key_idea: Quantifies Preference Mode Collapse via IDS, ASC, SDI and PVS metrics over identity, style, layout and tone attributes on 3,200 curated prompts, detecting output homogenization in diffusion models.
sources.takeaway: Provides concrete, implementable metrics (intra-set diversity, attribute-specific collapse) to detect when a generator collapses onto one style/layout - directly usable as a per-batch gate.

sources.title: Diversity and Novelty: Measurement, Learning and Optimization (UMD dissertation)
sources.key_idea: Proposes an entropy-based diversity metric (more accurate/sensitive than benchmarks) and learns triplet embeddings from human judgments to measure novelty of a design item.
sources.takeaway: Structural entropy of a design set is a principled diversity gate; embedding-based novelty (triplet/contrastive) complements nearest-neighbor distance for composition/typography fingerprinting.

topics.topic: (d) LLM / vision-model visual critique: feasibility and limits

sources.title: Can Multimodal Large Language Models Understand Graphic Design? A Comparative Study
sources.key_idea: Proposes a three-level evaluation framework (recognition, semantic, overall) plus an image-to-text benchmark of 8 tasks to measure MLLM alignment with human judgments of graphic design.
sources.takeaway: MLLMs can be structured to critique design at element/relation/whole levels - feasible as automated critique, but must be benchmarked against humans per level.

sources.title: From concept to manufacturing: evaluating vision-language models for design (GPT-4V benchmark)
sources.key_idea: Ran >1,000 queries evaluating GPT-4V across nine design tasks including design similarity, sketch description, engineering-drawing/CAD understanding, and manufacturability assessment.
sources.takeaway: GPT-4V is usable for design-similarity and critique tasks but accuracy varies strongly by subtask - good as a screening critic, not a sole judge.

sources.title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with LLM-as-a-Judge (LLM-as-a-Judge, Zheng et al.)
sources.key_idea: Establishes the LLM-as-a-judge paradigm and documents its systematic biases (position, verbosity, self-enhancement) and the need for calibration/pairwise comparison.
sources.takeaway: LLM critique is scalable and feasible but biased - design evaluation must use debiased, pairwise/calibrated judging, not a single uncalibrated score.

sources.title: MLLM-Bench: Evaluating Multi-modal LLMs using GPT-4V as a Judge
sources.key_idea: Uses GPT-4V as a judge to compare multimodal LLMs across user-experience dimensions, revealing significant performance gaps between models.
sources.takeaway: Vision-LLM-as-judge is a working pattern for design critique; the judge model itself must be validated, so pair it with metric gates rather than trusting it alone.

sources.title: An Empirical Evaluation of the GPT-4 Multimodal Model on Visualization Literacy Tasks
sources.key_idea: Empirically evaluates GPT-4V on visualization literacy (VLAT, chart QA, deceptive-design detection, visualization-design choices), establishing baseline performance.
sources.takeaway: Even strong VLMs have clear ceilings on design/layout reasoning - critique must be scoped to what the model reliably handles and combined with hard metric gates.

topics.topic: (e) 'Design memory' / avoiding repetition across generated artifacts

sources.title: DiverseGRPO: Mitigating Mode Collapse in Image Generation via Diversity-Aware Reward
sources.key_idea: Shows RL (GRPO) improves image-generation quality but later training homogenizes outputs (loss of creativity/diversity); proposes a diversity-aware reward based on group diversity.
sources.takeaway: Generative pipelines naturally drift toward repetition; a diversity term in the reward (or a post-hoc distinctness gate over recent outputs) is required to keep artifacts distinct.

sources.title: DivGAN: A diversity-enforcing generative adversarial network for mode collapse
sources.key_idea: Introduces DivNet, a module that enforces output diversity and alleviates mode collapse in any GAN without changing its architecture.
sources.takeaway: Diversity-enforcing components (a 'memory' of modes) prevent repetition and can be added as an anti-repetition module to a web-design generator.

sources.title: DivGenBench: Measuring Generative Diversity (Preference Mode Collapse)
sources.key_idea: Quantifies Preference Mode Collapse across identity, style, layout and tone, detecting when a generator collapses onto a narrow output region.
sources.takeaway: A rolling memory of recent outputs + PMC metrics (IDS/ASC/SDI/PVS) flags repetition and triggers regeneration/variation when collapse is detected.

sources.title: Embrace the Diversity: Avoiding Mode Collapse with Polarized Models (ICML 2025)
sources.key_idea: Shows that retraining on reward-selected synthetic data (e.g. maximizing a single alignment signal) can trigger mode collapse; diversity preservation is needed.
sources.takeaway: Optimizing toward one reward (e.g. a single 'aesthetic score') collapses variety - balance the reward with a coverage/diversity objective and a memory of the output distribution.

sources.title: NoveltyBench: Evaluating Language Models for Humanlike Diversity
sources.key_idea: Demonstrates models produce far fewer distinct outputs than humans and proposes distinct-k as the measurement; novelty scales inversely with model size.
sources.takeaway: Without explicit diversity pressure, generators repeat - measure distinct-k over the recent-output buffer to enforce variety and break template loops.

synthesis: Anti-template generation for BusinessForge should combine three layers, all grounded in the 2023-2026 literature above. (1) QUALITY GATE: automated aesthetic scoring is SOTA-feasible (Calista 2023; Appsthetics 2025 distributional view; AesthetiQ 2025 preference-alignment) and can be decomposed into measurable attributes (XAI/SHAP 2023) - score every candidate on layout balance, color harmony, typography and composition, treating aesthetic quality as a distribution not a single number. (2) DISTINCTNESS GATE (the core anti-template mechanism): treat novelty as a point metric = distance of a candidate to a reference corpus of prior/competitor/template designs, and diversity as a set metric over the batch (DeCoDe MIT metrics; Beyond Statistical Similarity 2023). Implement a 'design fingerprint' via embedding distance (CLIP/DINO or layout/attribute embeddings) to a memory of all previously generated artifacts; reject candidates whose nearest-neighbor distance or set entropy (UMD entropy metric 2019; DivGenBench IDS/ASC/SDI/PVS 2026) falls below threshold. Track distinct-k (NoveltyBench 2025) across the recent-output buffer to catch repetition early. (3) CRITIQUE LAYER: an MLLM critic is feasible and valuable (Microsoft 3-level framework 2026; Springer GPT-4V design-similarity benchmark 2025) but must be debiased and pairwise-calibrated (LLM-as-a-Judge 2023; MLLM-Bench 2023) and scoped to its proven strengths, never used as the sole judge (TVCG GPT-4V literacy baseline 2024). For the 'design memory' requirement specifically: no single paper coins that term, but the operational equivalent is well-established - maintain a persistent buffer/embedding index of all generated designs and apply diversity/novelty metrics as gates (DiverseGRPO 2025 diversity reward; DivGAN 2023 mode memory; ICML 2025 coverage objective; NoveltyBench 2025 distinct-k). Concrete pipeline: generate -> embed & compare to memory (novelty distance + batch entropy) -> MLLM critique on element/relation/whole levels -> aesthetic attribute scoring -> KEEP only if distinct AND high-quality AND critique-passing, else regenerate with a diversity nudge. Award-winning differentiators to actively engineer (Utsubo 2025; SliderRevolution 2024; DesignRush 2025): original concept, motion/interaction craft, narrative/storytelling and restraint - none of which a static Word-document template can ever satisfy, so the distinctness gate is what structurally prevents template-like output.
